report.summary: The change lets a required CI job with conclusion `skipped` pass the native merge gate. That goes against docs/10 Project CI.md, which requires every required job to be `success`. Jobs are marked `skipped` exactly when one of their needs failed, so a failing dependency now opens the gate for merges. No spec or IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES change goes with it (CLAUDE.md rule 16).

findings.text: The merge gate now treats a `skipped` required job as passed. The spec requires `success`, and `skipped` is the conclusion the runner gives a job whose need failed. So when a dependency of a required job fails or times out, the merge is allowed.

evidence.why: docs/10 Project CI.md:172: 'a native merge needs the newest run for the exact head SHA and the current revision, with every `required` job `success`.' docs/10 Project CI.md:84: 'If a need ends without success, the job completes as `skipped`.' This is implemented at repository-ci.ts:531-532 (`if (needs.some((need) => need?.status === "completed" && need.conclusion !== "success")) { this.completeJob(job, "skipped", ...`). Example: required job `deploy` needs `test`. `test` fails, so `deploy` becomes skipped and mergeBlock returns null, letting the merge through. The spec is unchanged and IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES records no deviation, which breaks CLAUDE.md rule 16. It also conflicts with CLOUDFLARE-CODE-HOSTING-PLAN.md:108 ('Empty, unknown, incomplete, cancelled, or stale required results cannot grant merge permission').

findings.text: Not blocking: none of the mergeBlock assertions (lines 256-291) has a required job ending as `skipped`. I didn't read the setup around those assertions to rule it out fully. With the spec's gate, the right test is a required job left skipped by a failed need, expecting mergeBlock to return the block message.

checked.risk: The spec: merge gate rule and job conclusion rules
Failure paths: guard must fail closed; how `skipped` is produced
Repository rules (spec change in same PR)
